A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CaDRe research work. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables, and rendered figures, support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting and added material.

before.justification: v2 reports original synthetic recovery experiments, climate causal-graph comparisons, forecasting results, and appendix ablations and scalability studies.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds experiments including CausalRivers evaluation, further baseline comparisons, dimensionality studies, and climate distribution diagnostics.

M1.justification: The CaDRe encoders, decoder, flow-based priors, objectives, structural penalties, and Jacobian-based graph extraction remain unchanged. The MICN backbone and proposed sliding-window extension were already documented in v2; the new architecture diagram redisplays existing components.

E1.justification: v3 adds CausalRivers evaluation with established reference causal relations, substantially extending real-world causal validation beyond wind surrogates, and adds an ENSO teleconnection case study. The climate datasets and ILI, ECL, and Traffic forecasting coverage already present in v2 are retained.

E2.justification: Synthetic causal-discovery comparisons newly evaluate DYNOTEARS, CUTS, Rhino, and Jacobian-CD in Figure 8, plus BIC and Generalized Score Function in Table 16. Figure 9 also includes VAR on CausalRivers. Existing forecasting and temporal representation-learning comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: New evaluations introduce AUROC/AUPRC on synthetic data and AUROC/F1-max on CausalRivers. Additional settings extend latent dimensions to 12, masked observation dimensions to 1000, and lag lengths to 5, and test estimated latent dimensionality. These are added protocols, without evidence that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds latent-dimension misspecification tests, broader dimensionality and lag sensitivity studies, Traffic and ENSO graph case studies, and quantile-based climate diagnostics addressing A2/A3. The existing assumption-violation, hyperparameter, and second-order dynamics analyses remain; they are not new additions.

E5.justification: Figures 13 and 14 newly report 95% confidence intervals for conditional means. Existing three-seed forecasting and five-seed synthetic reporting practices are retained, with no explicit increase in repeated-run counts. The confidence-interval construction is not specified.

E6.justification: Matching main result tables and retained appendix tables preserve their numerical values. v3 substantially expands results through new comparator scores, CausalRivers findings, dimensionality experiments, and diagnostics; for example, the added masked dx = 1000 setting reports SHD 0.19 ± 0.08.

T1.justification: The principal identifiability theorems, assumptions, SEM–ICA equivalence, and higher-order and observed-lag derivations are retained. Added discussion of continuous-support relabeling and the Hu–Schennach connection elaborates the existing reasoning without changing the formal guarantees or derivation steps.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contribution: joint nonparametric identification of latent dynamics and observed causal structure through CaDRe, supported by synthetic recovery and competitive climate forecasting.

C2.justification: The climate discussion changes claims of physical validation and causal influence into plausibility and association language. New discussions address finite-sample optimization, assumption failure modes, cross-domain latent meanings, forecasting mechanisms, and indirect assumption testing. These substantially expand and revise interpretation.

D1.justification: v3 newly supplies a code-access URL and clarifies that Table 5 uses prediction horizons with input length fixed at 96. It documents the new Traffic visualization threshold. Converting architecture Table A7 into Figure 7 retains the modules but omits some explicit tensor-shape details.

R1.justification: v3 expands noisy-CRL and forecasting literature, details its dependence on and adaptations of Hu and Schennach in Table 7, and replaces generic impact discussion with claims of adoption by six subsequent studies. These positioning changes go beyond bibliographic publication updates.

P1.justification: v3 introduces a standalone main-text Related Work section, places synthetic experiments under Section 4.1, and separates real-world experiments into Section 6.1. Rewritten conclusion and impact material and expanded explanatory passages substantially reorganize the narrative.

P2.justification: The main text and references change from single-column to two-column layout. The architecture table becomes a diagram, duplicated dimensionality tables are consolidated, and new comparison, diagnostic, and ENSO figures are added. Figure 12 also redisplays existing climate maps without rotation.

improvement.justification: CausalRivers evaluation, broader synthetic comparators, and ranking metrics address gaps in v2's causal validation, while several climate interpretations become more cautious. The gain is limited by sparse documentation of new protocols and overinterpretation of Figures 13–14: their dependence diagnostics do not establish the full identifiability assumptions they are labelled as verifying.
